name: FLORES-200
description: FLORES-200 is a benchmark dataset for machine translation between English and low-resource languages. It consists of 3001 sentences extracted from 842 distinct web articles, covering a variety of topics and domains. These sentences have been professionally translated into 200 languages, enabling evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems. The dataset is divided into three splits: dev, devtest, and test.

dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia, covering three domains: Wikinews (international news articles), Wikijunior (age-appropriate nonfiction books for children), and WikiVoyage (travel guides). The sentence selection process involved selecting an article at random from each source, then manually selecting 3-5 contiguous sentences from each article. Sentences were balanced across document locations (beginning, middle, end). The selection was performed by 10 annotators with diverse backgrounds and regions of origin.
dataBiases: The authors note that source sentences are extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into other languages, which introduces translationese effects. While the authors conjecture these effects are marginal when evaluating low-resource language models, the dataset inherently reflects English-centric content and perspectives. The selection of topics and domains (news, children's books, travel) may not represent all cultural contexts equally.
